title: Paramartha Guru Tale 91
summary: A rumor spread that a wild leopard had been seen in the forest outskirts.
full_text:
A rumor spread that a wild leopard had been seen in the forest outskirts.

Guru Paramartha instructed Peedan: 'Predators are terrified of sacred sounds! If you hear a rustle in the bushes tonight, beat the brass gong with all your might!'

At midnight, a stray goat rustled in the garden bushes.

Peedan seized the brass gong and an iron rod, beating it like thunder: CLANG! CLANG! CLANG!

The deafening noise awakened the entire village. It also awakened the local watchdogs, who began barking in chorus.

The real leopard, resting peacefully in the forest three miles away, was intrigued by the commotion. Attracted by the noise, the predator walked into the village to investigate!

Seeing the spotted beast stroll past the gate, Peedan dropped his gong, dove beneath his cot, and prayed: 'The gong was too melodious; it invited the guest instead of driving him away!'

The leopard caught a chicken from the coop and trotted back to the hills.

The Guru concluded: 'Next time, Peedan, we shall use silent meditation; it has fewer acoustic repercussions.'
moral: Ringing bells to frighten predators only summons them to the feast.

quiz.question: What is the central moral lesson taught in "Paramartha Guru Tale 91"?
options: Foolishness of book knowledge without worldly wisdom
Acting in haste and anger without thinking
Believing rumors and flattery without proof
quiz.hint: Remember the moral lesson of this traditional story.

quiz.question: How do the characters overcome their challenge?
options: Through patience, calm reflection, and wisdom
By shouting loudly and blaming others
By running away from every problem
quiz.hint: Consider the virtues praised in world folklore.

quiz.question: What memorable conclusion does this story teach young readers?
options: Honesty, kindness, and clear thinking lead to peace
quiz.hint: Reflect upon the resolution of the story.
